findings: Hardcoded modal detail labels — DriverDetail, PassengerDetail, and TripDetail all use plain English string literals as row labels (e.g. 'Name', 'License #', 'Account Status', 'Vehicle Type', 'Trip ID', 'Passenger Phone', etc.) instead of t() calls. Roughly 40 visible strings bypass i18n entirely. Replace each literal with a t('th_...') or a dedicated key.

Hardcoded status options in Trips filter — The <select> in Trips.tsx (lines 121–125) uses bare English option text ('Pending', 'Accepted', 'In Progress', 'Completed', 'Cancelled') and a hardcoded tooltip ('Trip is already in a terminal state', line 279). Replace with t('status_...') keys that already exist in i18n.ts.

Unguarded parseInt on limit/offset — In the trips endpoint (admin.ts lines 241–242), parseInt(limit as string, 10) and parseInt(offset as string, 10) produce NaN if the caller passes a non-numeric value. PostgreSQL rejects NaN parameters and returns a 500. Add isNaN checks and fall back to the defaults (50 and 0).

Unban not implemented — The i18n file defines unban/Ondoa Zuio keys and the plan included unban actions, but no backend endpoint (PUT /admin/drivers/:id/unban, PUT /admin/passengers/:id/unban) and no frontend call exist. Either add the endpoints or remove the translation keys to avoid dead UI surface in a future iteration.

Build evidence missing — A dist/ folder is present but the commit message contains no TypeScript compiler output and there is no CI log. The build command is 'tsc && vite build', so a type error would block the dist. Note this as unverified if deploying to staging requires a confirmed clean compile.
